entities.name: Soil-Transmitted Helminths
entities.description: A major cluster of neglected tropical intestinal nematode infections transmitted through human contact with fecally contaminated soil, predominantly comprising Ascaris lumbricoides, Trichuris trichiura, hookworms (Necator americanus and Ancylostoma duodenale), and Strongyloides stercoralis. The infections manifest with acute transpulmonary larval migration, chronic microcytic iron-deficiency anemia, protein-losing enteropathy, mechanical intestinal or hepatobiliary obstruction, trichuris dysentery with rectal prolapse, and life-threatening disseminated strongyloidiasis in immunosuppressed hosts.

entities.name: Fecal-Oral Ingestion of Infective Embryonated Eggs from Contaminated Soil or Food
entities.description: Transmission pathway involving the oral ingestion of infective embryonated eggs of Ascaris lumbricoides or Trichuris trichiura from fecally contaminated agricultural soil, unwashed vegetables and fruit, contaminated water, or soil-soiled hands, common in environments utilizing untreated human nightsoil.

entities.name: Percutaneous Penetration by Infective Filariform Larvae in Warm Moist Soil
entities.description: Direct transcutaneous inoculation pathway where free-living, infective third-stage filariform larvae of hookworms (Necator americanus, Ancylostoma duodenale) or Strongyloides stercoralis actively bore through bare human skin (typically feet, toes, or ankles) walking or resting on warm, shaded, fecally contaminated ground.

entities.name: Rural Tropical and Subtropical Communities with Inadequate Sanitation and Open Defecation
entities.description: Environmental exposure characterized by residence in or travel through impoverished rural tropical and subtropical regions lacking basic latrines, municipal wastewater infrastructure, or clean drinking water, where frequent open defecation sustains intense environmental contamination with helminth ova and larvae.

entities.name: Immunosuppressive State or Systemic Corticosteroid Therapy Predisposing to Hyperinfection
entities.description: Host predisposing condition of impaired cell-mediated immunity—most notably high-dose systemic corticosteroid administration, immunosuppressive antineoplastic chemotherapy, organ transplantation, or HTLV-1 co-infection—triggering accelerated Strongyloides stercoralis autoinfection leading to lethal disseminated hyperinfection syndrome.

entities.name: Ascaris lumbricoides
entities.description: The giant intestinal nematode roundworm measuring 15 to 35 cm in length that inhabits the lumen of the jejunum and ileum. Adult females produce up to 200,000 thick-shelled mammillated eggs per day, and large aggregated worm burdens cause mechanical intestinal occlusion or erratic migration into the biliary tree.

entities.name: Trichuris trichiura
entities.description: The human whipworm measuring 3 to 5 cm in length, possessing an attenuated, whip-like anterior three-fifths that embeds securely within cecal and colonic mucosal syncytia, producing characteristic barrel-shaped eggs with bipolar plugs and causing mucosal inflammation and capillary hemorrhage.

entities.name: Necator americanus
entities.description: The New World intestinal hookworm (8 to 11 mm cylindrical nematode) possessing paired semilunar cutting plates in its buccal capsule, attaching securely to duodenal and jejunal mucosa, lacerating capillaries, and ingesting approximately 0.03 to 0.05 mL of host blood per worm daily.

entities.name: Ancylostoma duodenale
entities.description: The Old World hookworm (10 to 13 mm cylindrical nematode) equipped with ventral pairs of curved cutting teeth, attaching to the upper small intestine and causing severe mucosal blood loss of up to 0.2 mL of host blood per worm daily, leading to rapid iron and protein depletion.

entities.name: Strongyloides stercoralis
entities.description: A minute intestinal threadworm (2 mm parthenogenetic parasitic female) residing in duodenal mucosa that undergoes an endogenous autoinfective cycle where rhabditiform larvae transform internally into infectious filariform larvae, enabling decades-long persistent infections without environmental re-exposure.

entities.name: Ground Itch Papulovesicular Pruritic Dermatitis
entities.description: Intensely pruritic, erythematous, papular or vesicular dermatologic eruption arising on the dorsum of the feet, soles, or interdigital webbing at the exact anatomical site of cutaneous hookworm larval penetration within hours to days of contact with infested soil.

entities.name: Larva Currens Rapidly Advancing Serpiginous Urticarial Wheal
entities.description: Pathognomonic cutaneous hallmark of Strongyloides stercoralis autoinfection, presenting as an excruciatingly itchy, raised, erythematous, linear serpiginous urticarial wheal that advances at a remarkably rapid velocity of 5 to 10 cm per hour over the perianal area, buttocks, thighs, or trunk.

entities.name: Rectal Prolapse Studded with White Whipworms in Trichuris Dysentery Syndrome
entities.description: Pathognomonic physical hallmark of severe pediatric whipworm infection (Trichuris Dysentery Syndrome), characterized by edematous, hyperemic rectal mucosa prolapsing through the anal sphincter during painful defecation, visibly encrusted with dozens of embedded white, thread-like adult Trichuris trichiura worms.

entities.name: Mechanical Bowel Obstruction with Palpable Doughy Abdominal Mass from Ascaris Worm Bolus
entities.description: Acute mechanical intestinal obstruction seen in young children harboring massive worm burdens (>100 to >1,000 adult roundworms) that aggregate into a solid luminal bolus occluding the ileocecal valve, manifesting with colicky abdominal pain, bilious vomiting, obstipation, and a moveable, non-tender doughy mass on abdominal palpation.

entities.name: Erratic Biliary Ascariasis with Acute Suppurative Cholangitis or Biliary Colic
entities.description: Severe hepatobiliary complication arising when adult Ascaris roundworms erratically migrate into the ampulla of Vater and common bile duct, precipitating excruciating right upper quadrant biliary colic, acute suppurative cholangitis, acute pancreatitis, or hepatic microabscesses.

entities.name: Löffler Syndrome Transient Eosinophilic Pulmonary Infiltrates
entities.description: Acute hypersensitivity pneumonitis occurring during the transpulmonary migration of helminth larvae (Ascaris, hookworms, Strongyloides) breaking through alveolar capillaries, presenting with dry hacking cough, burning substernal pain, wheezing, dyspnea, and transient migratory radiographic infiltrates.

entities.name: Severe Microcytic Hypochromic Iron Deficiency Anemia from Chronic Hookworm Blood Loss
entities.description: Profound hypochromic microcytic anemia on admission complete blood count (hemoglobin < 7 g/dL, often 3–6 g/dL; MCV < 70 fL; serum ferritin < 10 ng/mL; elevated TIBC) accompanied by hypoalbuminemia (< 2.5 g/dL) caused by cumulative capillary blood extraction and protein-losing enteropathy from adult hookworms.

entities.name: Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia during Larval Tissue Migration and Strongyloidiasis
entities.description: Marked elevation in peripheral eosinophil percentage and absolute count (20% to 50% during acute Löffler larval pulmonary migration; persistent 10% to 25% in chronic Strongyloides autoinfection), signaling systemic tissue-invasive helminthic immune activation.

entities.name: Diagnostic Stool Microscopy Demonstrating Characteristic Helminth Eggs or Rhabditiform Larvae
entities.description: Definitive admission parasitological identification in stool via Kato-Katz smear or Baermann concentration showing mammillated thick-shelled Ascaris eggs (45–75 x 35–50 um), barrel-shaped Trichuris eggs with bipolar mucoid plugs (50–55 x 22–24 um), thin-shelled hookworm eggs containing morulae (60–75 x 35–40 um), or motile Strongyloides rhabditiform larvae (200–300 um).

entities.name: Abdominal Ultrasound Inner Tube Sign or Tangled Spaghetti Pattern
entities.description: Admission bedside ultrasonography demonstrating either non-shadowing, linear, hyperechoic tubular structures with an anechoic central longitudinal line ('strip sign' / 'inner tube sign') actively writhing within the common bile duct, or clustered acoustic shadowing tubular loops ('whirlpool' / 'tangled spaghetti sign') inside obstructed bowel.

entities.name: Abdominal Radiography Railroad Track Linear Intestinal Filling Defects
entities.description: Admission plain abdominal radiography showing dilated bowel loops with multiple air-fluid levels, and barium contrast outlining distinctive parallel longitudinal linear filling defects ('railroad track sign') corresponding to adult roundworms in the small intestinal lumen.

entities.name: Absence of Helminth Eggs and Larvae on Multiple Concentrated Stool Examinations
entities.description: Total absence of parasitic ova and larvae across three serial concentrated fecal examinations using Kato-Katz thick smear, formalin-ether concentration, and Baermann funnel techniques in an immunocompetent patient, which definitively excludes symptomatic moderate-to-heavy soil-transmitted helminthiasis.

entities.name: Normal Hemoglobin Ferritin and Absolute Eosinophil Count
entities.description: Normal hemoglobin concentration (>12 g/dL), normal serum ferritin (>30 ng/mL), and normal absolute eosinophil count, the presence of which makes moderate-to-heavy hookworm disease and active invasive tissue helminthiasis virtually impossible.

entities.name: Absence of Environmental Exposure to Fecally Contaminated Soil or Endemic Transmission Zones
entities.description: Confirmed absence of residence or travel to rural tropical/subtropical endemic areas with inadequate sanitation and lack of personal contact with nightsoil, unwashed produce, or barefoot soil walking, rendering soil-transmitted helminth transmission epidemiologically implausible.

entities.name: Nutritional Iron Deficiency Anemia
entities.description: Microcytic hypochromic anemia stemming strictly from inadequate dietary iron intake, poor iron bioavailability, or physiologic increased requirements without parasitic enteric blood loss.

entities.name: Inflammatory Bowel Disease
entities.description: Idiopathic autoimmune chronic inflammatory colitis (Ulcerative Colitis or Crohn's Disease) causing recurrent bloody mucoid diarrhea, tenesmus, abdominal cramping, and rectal mucosal inflammation in children and young adults.

entities.name: Cutaneous Scabies Infestation
entities.description: Contagious parasitic infestation of the epidermis by Sarcoptes scabiei mites presenting with pruritic burrow tracks, erythematous papules, and severe nocturnal itching.

entities.name: Acute Mechanical Bowel Obstruction from Intussusception or Volvulus
entities.description: Non-helminthic mechanical pediatric intestinal obstruction caused by telescoping of the bowel (ileocolic intussusception) or midgut twisting (volvulus) presenting with acute colicky abdominal pain, vomiting, and obstipation.

entities.name: Choledocholithiasis and Acute Bacterial Cholangitis
entities.description: Biliary tract obstruction produced by radiopaque or cholesterol gallstones impacted in the common bile duct, precipitating Charcot's triad of right upper quadrant pain, fever, and jaundice.

entities.name: Single-Dose Oral Albendazole 400 mg
entities.description: Standard WHO first-line anthelmintic regimen comprising a single oral dose of 400 mg albendazole (200 mg for toddlers 12–24 months), which binds parasite beta-tubulin, achieving >95% cure rates against Ascaris lumbricoides and >80% cure against hookworms.

entities.name: Oral Mebendazole 500 mg Single Dose or 100 mg Twice Daily for Three Days
entities.description: First-line benzimidazole anthelmintic regimen delivering mebendazole 500 mg single dose or 100 mg BID for 3 days, providing superior efficacy against Trichuris trichiura and significant clearance of adult Ascaris roundworms.

entities.name: Oral Ivermectin 200 mcg per kg for Two Doses
entities.description: Highly specific macrocyclic lactone anthelmintic administered orally at 200 mcg/kg/day for 2 consecutive days, achieving >95% cure rates against Strongyloides stercoralis by opening glutamate-gated chloride channels, and serving as essential therapy for refractory Trichuris trichiura when paired with albendazole.

entities.name: Intrinsic Resistance and Refractoriness of Strongyloides stercoralis to Benzimidazole Monotherapy
entities.description: Inherent biological tolerance and clinical failure of Strongyloides stercoralis when treated with standard single-dose or short-course albendazole or mebendazole, which fail to achieve parasitological cure and permit continuous life-threatening autoinfection.

entities.name: Oral Ferrous Sulfate Iron Replacement Therapy
entities.description: Adjuvant oral iron supplementation (3 to 6 mg elemental iron/kg/day in children; 200 mg three times daily in adults) maintained for 3 months following anthelmintic deworming to fully replenish depleted bone marrow iron stores.

entities.name: Conservative Decompression and Piperazine Citrate for Ascaris Intestinal Obstruction
entities.description: Conservative non-surgical therapeutic protocol comprising nasogastric decompression, fluid resuscitation, and oral piperazine citrate (which flaccidly paralyzes adult Ascaris worms via GABA-receptor agonism) allowing spontaneous peristaltic clearance of the obstructing worm mass.

entities.name: Refractoriness to Standard Antibacterial and Antifungal Therapies
entities.description: Clinical failure of empiric broad-spectrum antibacterial or antifungal medications to eliminate helminthic infection, manifested by unremitting eosinophilia, ongoing gastrointestinal symptoms, and persistent fecal egg excretion.

relationships.target: Rural Tropical and Subtropical Communities with Inadequate Sanitation and Open Defecation
relationships.keywords: tropical endemicity, open defecation, inadequate sanitation, rural poverty, environmental contamination
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Soil-Transmitted Helminths infections are concentrated in impoverished rural tropical and subtropical regions where open defecation and the absence of municipal sanitary facilities lead to continuous contamination of the living environment with helminth ova and larvae.

relationships.keywords: immunosuppression, corticosteroid risk, HTLV-1 co-infection, accelerated autoinfection, hyperinfection trigger
relationships.description: [EXPOSURE_TO] Soil-Transmitted Helminths (specifically Strongyloides stercoralis) progress to life-threatening hyperinfection syndrome and dissemination when exposed to host immunosuppressive conditions, particularly systemic corticosteroid therapy or HTLV-1 co-infection.

relationships.target: Ancylostoma duodenale
relationships.keywords: Old World hookworm, etiologic agent, ventral teeth, mucosal hemorrhage

relationships.target: Strongyloides stercoralis

relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGEN] Soil-Transmitted Helminths include strongyloidiasis caused by Strongyloides stercoralis, an intestinal nematode uniquely capable of lifelong internal autoinfection and catastrophic dissemination.

relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Soil-Transmitted Helminths produce 'ground itch'—an intensely pruritic, papulovesicular dermatitis at the dermal penetration sites of hookworm filariform larvae on the dorsum of feet and toes.

relationships.keywords: larva currens, pathognomonic rash, rapid migration, urticarial wheal, Strongyloides hallmark
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Soil-Transmitted Helminths (specifically Strongyloides stercoralis) produce larva currens, a pathognomonic raised, erythematous, serpiginous linear wheal advancing at 5 to 10 cm per hour across the perianal skin, buttocks, and thighs.

relationships.target: Rectal Prolapse Studded with White Whipworms in Trichuris Dysentery Syndrome
relationships.keywords: rectal prolapse, visible whipworms, Trichuris dysentery syndrome, pathognomonic hallmark, pediatric tenesmus
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Soil-Transmitted Helminths (specifically heavy Trichuris trichiura infection in children) cause Trichuris Dysentery Syndrome with pathognomonic rectal prolapse displaying hyperemic mucosa visibly studded with dozens of white, thread-like adult whipworms.

relationships.target: Mechanical Bowel Obstruction with Palpable Doughy Abdominal Mass from Ascaris Worm Bolus
relationships.keywords: mechanical bowel obstruction, worm bolus, doughy mass, ileocecal obstruction, Ascaris mass
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Soil-Transmitted Helminths (specifically massive Ascaris lumbricoides burdens in young children) cause acute mechanical bowel obstruction where hundreds of coiled worms form an intraluminal bolus, presenting with bilious vomiting, abdominal distension, and a moveable, doughy abdominal mass.

relationships.target: Erratic Biliary Ascariasis with Acute Suppurative Cholangitis or Biliary Colic
relationships.keywords: biliary ascariasis, wandering worms, ampulla of Vater, suppurative cholangitis, biliary colic
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Soil-Transmitted Helminths feature erratic migration of adult Ascaris into the ampulla of Vater, presenting as acute right upper quadrant biliary colic, suppurative cholangitis, acute pancreatitis, or hepatic microabscesses.

relationships.target: Löffler Syndrome Transient Eosinophilic Pulmonary Infiltrates
relationships.keywords: Löffler syndrome, transpulmonary migration, eosinophilic pneumonitis, dry cough, fleeting infiltrates
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Soil-Transmitted Helminths provoke Löffler syndrome during transpulmonary larval migration, characterized by dry hacking cough, wheezing, substernal burning pain, marked peripheral eosinophilia, and migratory pulmonary infiltrates on chest radiography.

relationships.target: Severe Microcytic Hypochromic Iron Deficiency Anemia from Chronic Hookworm Blood Loss
relationships.keywords: microcytic hypochromic anemia, severe iron deficiency, low ferritin, hookworm blood loss, hypoalbuminemia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Soil-Transmitted Helminths (specifically chronic hookworm infection) exhibit profound microcytic hypochromic iron-deficiency anemia (hemoglobin < 7 g/dL, MCV < 70 fL, ferritin < 10 ng/mL) and hypoalbuminemia (< 2.5 g/dL) due to ongoing intestinal blood loss and protein-losing enteropathy.

relationships.target: Peripheral Blood Eosinophilia during Larval Tissue Migration and Strongyloidiasis
relationships.keywords: peripheral eosinophilia, larval migration, tissue invasion, strongyloidiasis eosinophilia, Löffler eosinophilia
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Soil-Transmitted Helminths characteristically demonstrate marked peripheral blood eosinophilia (20% to 50% during acute Löffler larval migration; persistent 10% to 25% in chronic Strongyloides infection) reflecting tissue-invasive larval immune responses.

relationships.target: Diagnostic Stool Microscopy Demonstrating Characteristic Helminth Eggs or Rhabditiform Larvae
relationships.keywords: stool microscopy, Kato-Katz smear, Baermann technique, mammillated eggs, bipolar plugs, rhabditiform larvae
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Soil-Transmitted Helminths exhibit diagnostic hallmark parasitological patterns on admission stool microscopy: mammillated eggs (Ascaris), barrel-shaped bipolar-plugged eggs (Trichuris), thin-shelled morulated eggs (hookworms), or motile rhabditiform larvae on Baermann funnel / agar plate (Strongyloides).

relationships.target: Abdominal Ultrasound Inner Tube Sign or Tangled Spaghetti Pattern
relationships.keywords: bedside ultrasound, inner tube sign, strip sign, tangled spaghetti sign, biliary ascariasis ultrasound
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Soil-Transmitted Helminths display characteristic bedside abdominal ultrasound patterns: non-shadowing tubular hyperechoic structures with an anechoic central lumen ('inner tube / strip sign') in biliary ascariasis, and clustered acoustic interfaces ('tangled spaghetti sign') in intestinal obstruction.

relationships.target: Abdominal Radiography Railroad Track Linear Intestinal Filling Defects
relationships.keywords: abdominal radiograph, air-fluid levels, barium contrast, railroad track sign, intestinal roundworms
relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Soil-Transmitted Helminths exhibit plain abdominal radiographic findings of small bowel obstruction with air-fluid levels, and barium contrast outlining parallel longitudinal linear filling defects ('railroad track sign') created by adult roundworms in the intestinal lumen.

relationships.target: Absence of Helminth Eggs and Larvae on Multiple Concentrated Stool Examinations
relationships.keywords: rule-out criterion, negative stool exams, Kato-Katz negative, Baermann negative, exclusion of helminthiasis
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Heavy symptomatic Soil-Transmitted Helminths infection is ruled out by the documented absence of helminth eggs and larvae on multiple serial concentrated stool examinations using both Kato-Katz thick smear and Baermann concentration techniques in an immunocompetent patient.

relationships.target: Normal Hemoglobin Ferritin and Absolute Eosinophil Count
relationships.keywords: rule-out criterion, normal hemoglobin, normal ferritin, normal eosinophils, exclusion of hookworm
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Heavy hookworm disease and active invasive tissue helminthiasis are ruled out by entirely normal admission hemoglobin (>12 g/dL), normal serum ferritin (>30 ng/mL), and normal absolute eosinophil count.

relationships.target: Absence of Environmental Exposure to Fecally Contaminated Soil or Endemic Transmission Zones
relationships.keywords: rule-out criterion, zero exposure, non-endemic, sanitation adequate, epidemiological exclusion
relationships.description: [RULED_OUT_BY] Soil-Transmitted Helminths are ruled out by the definitive lack of environmental exposure, including no lifetime travel or residence in endemic tropical/subtropical regions lacking sanitation and zero contact with unwashed soil-grown foods or nightsoil.

relationships.target: Nutritional Iron Deficiency Anemia
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, dietary iron deficiency, non-parasitic anemia, absent eosinophilia, negative stool
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths are differentiated from nutritional iron deficiency anemia because nutritional anemia lacks hookworm eggs on stool microscopy, lacks peripheral eosinophilia, and achieves permanent hematological cure with oral iron alone without anthelmintic therapy.

relationships.target: Inflammatory Bowel Disease
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, ulcerative colitis, Crohn disease, Trichuris dysentery, non-parasitic colitis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths (Trichuris Dysentery Syndrome) are differentiated from inflammatory bowel disease because IBD demonstrates chronic mucosal or transmural inflammation without visible parasites on endoscopy, lacks bipolar-plugged eggs on stool microscopy, and fails to resolve with benzimidazole anthelmintics.

relationships.target: Cutaneous Scabies Infestation
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, Sarcoptes scabiei, scabies burrows, larva currens contrast, stationary lesions
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths (Strongyloides larva currens) are differentiated from cutaneous scabies because scabies burrows are stationary and favor interdigital web spaces and wrists with nocturnal pruritus, whereas larva currens is a hyper-mobile urticarial wheal migrating rapidly at 5 to 10 cm per hour over the perianal skin and trunk.

relationships.target: Acute Mechanical Bowel Obstruction from Intussusception or Volvulus
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, pediatric bowel obstruction, idiopathic intussusception, midgut volvulus, absence of worm bolus
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths are differentiated from idiopathic intussusception or volvulus because non-parasitic mechanical obstructions lack intraluminal tubular masses ('tangled spaghetti' / 'railroad track' signs) on ultrasonography/radiography and do not expel adult Ascaris roundworms.

relationships.target: Choledocholithiasis and Acute Bacterial Cholangitis
relationships.keywords: differential diagnosis, gallstone obstruction, biliary colic, acoustic shadowing, non-parasitic cholangitis
relationships.description: [DIFFERENTIATED_FROM] Soil-Transmitted Helminths (biliary ascariasis) are differentiated from choledocholithiasis because gallstone obstruction displays acoustic-shadowing calculi on ultrasound without motile tubular non-shadowing structures ('inner tube sign'), and lacks expelled adult worms or helminth eggs.

relationships.target: Single-Dose Oral Albendazole 400 mg
relationships.keywords: first-line anthelmintic, albendazole 400 mg, roundworm cure, hookworm clearance, beta-tubulin inhibitor
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Soil-Transmitted Helminths show high therapeutic responsiveness to a single oral dose of albendazole 400 mg, achieving >95% cure rates for Ascaris lumbricoides and >80% cure rates for hookworms, rapidly eliminating intestinal worm burdens.

relationships.target: Oral Mebendazole 500 mg Single Dose or 100 mg Twice Daily for Three Days
relationships.keywords: first-line anthelmintic, mebendazole, whipworm treatment, Trichuris clearance, multi-dose regimen
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Soil-Transmitted Helminths respond effectively to mebendazole 500 mg single dose or 100 mg BID for 3 days, providing superior clearance against Trichuris trichiura and prompt resolution of Trichuris Dysentery Syndrome.

relationships.target: Oral Ivermectin 200 mcg per kg for Two Doses
relationships.keywords: drug of choice, ivermectin, Strongyloides cure, larva currens resolution, hyperinfection therapy
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Soil-Transmitted Helminths (specifically Strongyloides stercoralis) respond exquisitely to oral ivermectin 200 mcg/kg/day for 2 consecutive days (>95% cure rate), rapidly halting larva currens and resolving chronic or disseminated strongyloidiasis.

relationships.target: Intrinsic Resistance and Refractoriness of Strongyloides stercoralis to Benzimidazole Monotherapy
relationships.keywords: intrinsic resistance, benzimidazole failure, Strongyloides insensitivity, albendazole failure, autoinfection persistence
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Soil-Transmitted Helminths (specifically Strongyloides stercoralis) exhibit intrinsic therapeutic refractoriness and low cure rates when treated with standard single-dose albendazole or mebendazole, allowing internal autoinfection to persist.

relationships.target: Oral Ferrous Sulfate Iron Replacement Therapy
relationships.keywords: iron replacement, oral ferrous sulfate, anemia resolution, hookworm rehabilitation, reticulocytosis
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Soil-Transmitted Helminths (hookworm-associated iron-deficiency anemia) demonstrate robust therapeutic hematological recovery and replenishment of bone marrow iron stores when treated with oral ferrous sulfate for 3 months following anthelmintic deworming.

relationships.target: Conservative Decompression and Piperazine Citrate for Ascaris Intestinal Obstruction
relationships.keywords: conservative management, piperazine citrate, flaccid paralysis, nasogastric decompression, worm bolus passage
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Partial mechanical bowel obstruction caused by Ascaris lumbricoides responds favorably to conservative nasogastric decompression and oral piperazine citrate, which flaccidly paralyzes adult worms and allows spontaneous evacuation without laparotomy.

relationships.target: Refractoriness to Standard Antibacterial and Antifungal Therapies
relationships.keywords: antibiotic refractoriness, antimicrobial insensitivity, antibacterial failure, persistent eosinophilia
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Soil-Transmitted Helminths do not respond to standard antibacterial or antifungal agents, displaying persistent eosinophilia, gastrointestinal symptoms, and ongoing fecal egg shedding unless targeted anthelmintic therapy is initiated.

relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Ascaris lumbricoides causes mechanical bowel obstruction when large worm burdens aggregate into a solid luminal bolus occluding the ileocecal valve in young children.

relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Ascaris lumbricoides migrates erratically through the ampulla of Vater into the biliary tree, causing biliary colic, acute cholangitis, or pancreatitis.

relationships.description: [EXHIBITS_LAB_PATTERN] Necator americanus causes severe microcytic hypochromic iron-deficiency anemia by lacerating duodenal capillaries with cutting plates and ingesting host blood.

relationships.keywords: pathogen hallmark, mucosal blood loss, buccal teeth laceration, microcytic anemia

relationships.target: Larva Currens Rapidly Advancing Serpiginous Urticarial Wheal
relationships.keywords: pathogen hallmark, rapid cutaneous migration, larva currens, autoinfection wheal
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Strongyloides stercoralis produces the pathognomonic rapidly advancing serpiginous urticarial eruption known as larva currens during subcutaneous larval autoinfection.

relationships.target: Intrinsic Resistance and Refractoriness of Strongyloides stercoralis to Benzimidazole Monotherapy
relationships.keywords: pathogen resistance, benzimidazole insensitivity, treatment failure, autoinfection persistence
relationships.description: [INTRINSICALLY_RESISTANT_TO] Strongyloides stercoralis is intrinsically refractoriness to standard single-dose benzimidazoles (albendazole and mebendazole), failing to achieve parasitological cure.

relationships.target: Oral Ivermectin 200 mcg per kg for Two Doses
relationships.keywords: pathogen targeted therapy, ivermectin sensitivity, macrocyclic lactone cure, Strongyloides eradication
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Strongyloides stercoralis responds with >95% cure rates to oral ivermectin 200 mcg/kg/day for 2 consecutive days, which terminates autoinfection and prevents fatal dissemination.

relationships.target: Single-Dose Oral Albendazole 400 mg
relationships.keywords: targeted therapy, high cure rate, Ascaris clearance, albendazole efficacy
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Ascaris lumbricoides is highly susceptible to single-dose oral albendazole 400 mg, achieving >95% parasitological cure and stool egg reduction.

relationships.target: Oral Mebendazole 500 mg Single Dose or 100 mg Twice Daily for Three Days
relationships.keywords: targeted therapy, Trichuris clearance, whipworm eradication, mebendazole efficacy
relationships.description: [RESPONDS_TO] Trichuris trichiura responds preferentially to oral mebendazole 500 mg single dose or 100 mg twice daily for 3 days, clearing adult whipworms from colonic mucosa.

relationships.target: Ground Itch Papulovesicular Pruritic Dermatitis
relationships.keywords: pathogen hallmark, larval skin invasion, ground itch, papulovesicular dermatitis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Necator americanus provokes intense pruritic ground itch papulovesicular dermatitis at the dermal site where infective filariform larvae penetrate the host's feet.

relationships.target: Ground Itch Papulovesicular Pruritic Dermatitis
relationships.keywords: pathogen hallmark, percutaneous entry, ground itch, foot dermatitis
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Ancylostoma duodenale causes ground itch dermatitis at dermal sites of larval skin penetration following contact with infested soil.

relationships.target: Löffler Syndrome Transient Eosinophilic Pulmonary Infiltrates
relationships.keywords: pathogen hallmark, larval pulmonary migration, transpulmonary transit, Löffler syndrome
relationships.description: [HAS_PATHOGNOMONIC_HALLMARK] Ascaris lumbricoides larvae trigger Löffler syndrome during transpulmonary migration, breaking through alveolar capillaries and provoking transient eosinophilic pulmonary infiltrates.
